info.title: MetricFlow Public API
info.description:
Public API for Facebook Ads analytics, campaign management, and automation.

## Authentication
Pass your API key via header:
```
X-API-Key: mf_live_...
```
or
```
Authorization: Bearer mf_live_...
```
Create keys in [Settings > API](/settings?form=api-keys).

## Scopes
| Scope | Access |
|---|---|
| `analytics:read` | Overview, summary, daily breakdown |
| `ad_accounts:read` | Ad accounts list with metrics |
| `campaigns:read` | Campaigns, adsets, ads, creatives |
| `rules:read` | Automation rules and history |
| `rules:write` | Create, update, delete and pause automation rules |
| `entities:write` | Pause/enable, budgets, duplicate |
| `bundles:read` | Bundle configs and logs |
| `bundles:write` | Pause/resume bundles |
| `seeding:read` | Comment seeding: tasks, queue, author pages, images (Pro plan and higher or a custom plan) |
| `seeding:write` | Comment seeding: create/update/start/pause/delete tasks, upload images (Pro plan and higher or a custom plan) |
| `pages:read` | Fan pages, their comments and stats, comment-history scan jobs |
| `pages:write` | Moderate comments, page settings, webhook subscription, queue comment-history scans |

## Rate Limits
- **Read:** 120 req/min
- **Write:** 10-30 req/min
- **Daily:** depends on plan (Starter: 1K, Growth: 2.5K, Pro: 5K, Business: 20K)

## Date Ranges
Use `from` and `to` query parameters in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Defaults to last 90 days.

## Comment history scan
Facebook pushes only NEW comments over webhooks, so a delivery gap leaves a hole in a page's comment history and nothing re-sends it. A scan walks the page's posts and ingests what the webhook missed:

- **Catch up after a gap** — `POST /api/v1/pages/{page_id}/backfill` with `{"lookback_hours": 6, "mode": "apply"}`. Cheap enough to schedule: the window is pushed to Facebook and only posts that can plausibly carry new comments (live ads, recently-commented posts, posts created inside the window) are walked.
- **Decide comment by comment** — `mode="review"` stops the job in status `review`. Read the verdicts from `GET /api/v1/pages/backfill-jobs/{job_id}/items`, then post your decision to `POST /api/v1/pages/backfill-review/apply`. While a job waits in `review` the page's cleaner is paused for those comments, for up to 24 hours — cancel any review you are not going to apply (`POST /api/v1/pages/backfill-jobs/{job_id}/cancel`).
- **First-time cleanup** — `lookback_days` (0 = all history) walks the page's entire ad-post history. Thorough and slow; not for a schedule.

Scans are queued: the endpoints return a job, poll it via `GET /api/v1/pages/backfill-jobs/{job_id}`. One page can be scanned once every 30 minutes (429 with `Retry-After`, or `skipped_details` with `reason="cooldown"` in a bulk call), and one account can hold 50 queued or running scans at a time. The endpoints themselves allow 10 req/min (single page) and 2 req/min (bulk, up to 50 pages per call).

## Errors
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | Bad request |
| 401 | Invalid API key |
| 402 | Subscription expired — every endpoint except /usage and /me |
| 403 | Missing scope |
| 404 | Not found |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded |

## Calling from a browser (CORS)
All `/api/v1/*` endpoints allow cross-origin requests from any origin (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) — no CORS proxy needed, and never route your key through one. Remember that a key embedded in client-side code is visible to anyone who can open the page: use a dedicated **read-only** key (`analytics:read` + `campaigns:read`) for browser dashboards and keep write-scoped keys server-side.

get.description:
One row per ``(ad_account, hierarchy entity, date)`` across many ad accounts in a single request — replaces the 4-step ``ad-accounts → campaigns → adsets → ads`` walk.

**Query parameters:**
* ``from`` / ``to`` — date range (YYYY-MM-DD), max 90 days.
* ``level`` — ``campaign`` (default), ``adset``, or ``ad``.
* ``ad_account_ids`` — comma-separated, e.g. ``act_123,act_456``. If omitted, includes every account you own.
* ``fields`` — comma-separated subset of metric fields. Metrics not listed are OMITTED from response rows entirely (they are not returned as null). Identifier and name columns are always returned. Allowed metric names: ``spend, impressions, clicks, reach, frequency, cpc, cpm, ctr, unique_clicks, inline_link_clicks, unique_inline_link_clicks, leads, purchases, registrations, video_views, app_installs, landing_page_views, conversions, video_3s_views, video_p100_views, video_starts, video_total_watch_time, hook_rate, hold_rate, video_avg_time_watched``. ``hook_rate``, ``hold_rate`` and ``video_avg_time_watched`` are derived (no DB column); asking for them auto-pulls their dependencies (`impressions`, `video_3s_views`, `video_p100_views`; `video_total_watch_time`, `video_starts`) so the response is self-contained.
* ``currency`` — ``usd`` (default) or ``native``. Controls the denomination of every monetary field (``spend``, ``cpc``, ``cpm``). USD values are computed as ``native × ad_account.currency_ratio_to_usd``; the ratio is also returned on each row so the client can convert the other way without a round-trip.
* ``limit`` — page size, default 100, max 100.
* ``cursor`` — opaque token from previous response's ``pagination.cursor``.

**Always-returned identifier / metadata columns** (in addition to the metric fields listed above):
* ``campaign_id`` / ``campaign_name`` — populated for every level.
* ``adset_id`` / ``adset_name`` — populated for ``adset`` and ``ad``.
* ``ad_id`` / ``ad_name`` — populated for ``ad``.
* ``status`` / ``effective_status`` — entity status at the requested level (ACTIVE / PAUSED / DISAPPROVED / ...).
* ``daily_budget`` / ``lifetime_budget`` — the entity's current budget (campaign at ``level=campaign`` (CBO), adset at ``level=adset`` (ABO); always null at ``level=ad``). It's the current value (not per-date) so it repeats across a campaign/adset's date rows. Honors ``?currency``.
* ``targeting_country`` (list of ISO codes), ``targeting_age`` (e.g. ``18-65``), ``targeting_gender`` (``all`` / ``male`` / ``female``) — populated for ``adset`` and ``ad`` levels.
* ``landing_url`` — primary landing URL (Ad.call_to_action_link). Populated only at ``level=ad``.
* ``url_tags`` — UTM-style query string Meta appends to clicks (e.g. ``utm_source=fb&utm_campaign=spring``). ``ad`` level only.
* ``app_link`` — app deep link / store URL for app-promo CTAs (``ad`` level only).
* ``call_to_action_type`` — CTA enum (SHOP_NOW / LEARN_MORE / INSTALL_APP / ...). ``ad`` level only.
* ``google_play_link`` — narrow subset of ``landing_url`` (only when the host is ``play.google.com``). Kept for backward compatibility — new integrations should prefer ``landing_url``.

**URL filters (ad level only)**:
* ``url_contains`` — case-insensitive substring on landing_url.
* ``utm_source`` / ``utm_campaign`` / ``utm_medium`` — substring on url_tags. Returns 400 when used with ``level != ad``.

**Pagination**: keyset-based. When ``pagination.has_more`` is true, pass ``pagination.cursor`` as ``?cursor=...`` to fetch the next page.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: Pass to next request as ``?cursor=`` to fetch the next page

daily_budget.title: Daily Budget
daily_budget.description: Daily budget of the entity (campaign at level=campaign, adset at level=adset). null at level=ad and when the entity uses a lifetime budget instead. **Unit:** the ad account currency's MINOR unit, exactly as Facebook returns it — a $1,300.00 budget on a USD account reads `130000`. Divide by 100, EXCEPT for the zero-decimal currencies (CLP, COP, CRC, HUF, IDR, ISK, JPY, KRW, PYG, TWD, VND), whose Facebook offset is 1: there the number is already whole. Note this differs from `spend`, `cpc` and `cpm` (major units) and from the write endpoints (`POST /entities/{id}/budget`, `/bid`), which take major units. With `?currency=usd` the value is multiplied by the FX ratio, which does NOT change the scale: you get USD cents on a 100-offset account and whole USD on a zero-decimal one.

lifetime_budget.title: Lifetime Budget
lifetime_budget.description: Lifetime budget of the entity. null at level=ad and when the entity uses a daily budget instead. **Unit:** the ad account currency's MINOR unit, exactly as Facebook returns it — a $1,300.00 budget on a USD account reads `130000`. Divide by 100, EXCEPT for the zero-decimal currencies (CLP, COP, CRC, HUF, IDR, ISK, JPY, KRW, PYG, TWD, VND), whose Facebook offset is 1: there the number is already whole. Note this differs from `spend`, `cpc` and `cpm` (major units) and from the write endpoints (`POST /entities/{id}/budget`, `/bid`), which take major units. With `?currency=usd` the value is multiplied by the FX ratio, which does NOT change the scale: you get USD cents on a 100-offset account and whole USD on a zero-decimal one.

landing_url.title: Landing Url
landing_url.description: Primary landing URL — Ad.call_to_action_link. Populated only for level=ad.

url_tags.title: Url Tags
url_tags.description: UTM-style query string Meta appends to clicks (e.g. utm_source=fb&utm_campaign=...). Ad level only.

app_link.title: App Link
app_link.description: App deep link / store URL for app-promo CTAs. Ad level only.

call_to_action_type.title: Call To Action Type
call_to_action_type.description: CTA enum (SHOP_NOW / LEARN_MORE / INSTALL_APP / ...). Ad level only.

currency_ratio_to_usd.title: Currency Ratio To Usd
currency_ratio_to_usd.description: Multiplier: native_value × ratio = USD. Returned regardless of the `currency` query param.

video_3s_views.title: Video 3S Views
video_3s_views.description: Video plays of at least 3 seconds (Meta `actions` → `video_view`) — matches Ads Manager's hook-rate numerator.

video_starts.title: Video Starts
video_starts.description: Video playback starts (Meta `video_play_actions`; with autoplay ≈ every impression). Denominator of `video_avg_time_watched`.

video_total_watch_time.title: Video Total Watch Time
video_total_watch_time.description: Total seconds watched = Σ(avg seconds × starts). Additive carrier of `video_avg_time_watched`: divide by `video_starts` for the weighted average at any grouping.

video_avg_time_watched.title: Video Avg Time Watched
video_avg_time_watched.description: Average seconds a video was watched, weighted by video plays across the rows (Meta `video_avg_time_watched_actions`). Ad level; null outside video. Aggregated as Σ(avg×plays)/Σ(plays), so parent rows are a true weighted average, not an average of averages.

hook_rate.title: Hook Rate
hook_rate.description: % of impressions that watched ≥3s — `video_3s_views / impressions × 100`. Computed only when both deps are selected (or `fields` is omitted).

hold_rate.title: Hold Rate
hold_rate.description: % of 3s-viewers who watched to 100% — `video_p100_views / video_3s_views × 100`. Computed only when both deps are selected (or `fields` is omitted).

InsightRow.title: InsightRow
InsightRow.description:
One flat insight row from ``GET /api/v1/insights``.

Hierarchy fields not relevant for the requested level come back as
``null`` (e.g. ``adset_id``/``ad_id`` when ``level=campaign``).
Metric fields not requested via ``?fields=...`` come back as
``null`` rather than being absent — that keeps the response shape
stable for OpenAPI consumers. Use ``response_model_exclude_none``
on a per-call basis if you need a smaller payload.
